title: Save Tax on Property Capital Gains: A Practical Guide
description: Selling a residential property after two years yields Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) subject to 20% tax with indexation benefit. You can claim exemption from .

faq.q: What is the difference between Short-Term and Long-Term Capital Gains on property?
faq.a: Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) arise if you sell a property within 24 months of purchase, and are added to your income and taxed at your slab rates. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) arise if you sell after 24 months, and are taxed at 20% with indexation benefits.

faq.q: Can I buy multiple properties to claim Section 54 exemption?
faq.a: Until recently, you could reinvest in two residential properties if the capital gains did not exceed ₹2 crores. However, for sales made on or after April 1, 2023, the exemption under Section 54 is limited to investing in *one* residential house property, with a maximum reinvestment cap of ₹10 crores.

faq.q: What if I don't use the money in the Capital Gains Account Scheme (CGAS)?
faq.a: Any amount deposited in CGAS that is not utilised for the purchase or construction of a new residential property within the specified time limits (2 or 3 years from the date of sale) will become taxable as LTCG in the financial year in which the time limit expires.

faq.q: Does Section 54 apply to Non-Resident Indians (NRIs)?
faq.a: Yes, Section 54 exemption is available to NRIs as well, provided they meet all the conditions, including reinvesting the capital gains in a residential property located in India.

faq.q: Can I claim Section 54 exemption if I already own multiple properties?
faq.a: Yes, there is no restriction on the number of properties you already own to claim Section 54 exemption. The condition is that you must reinvest the capital gains from the sale of one residential property into purchasing or constructing *one* new residential property in India within the specified timeframes.

faq.q: What documents are needed to open a CGAS account?
faq.a: Typically, you will need a copy of your PAN card, address proof, the acknowledgement of your Income Tax Return, and a declaration stating the purpose of the deposit and the amount of capital gains.

based_on.title: Sold a residential property? Here's how you can save tax on capital gains

fact_check.summary: The article provides largely accurate information regarding tax savings on property capital gains in India, including details on LTCG, Section 54, and CGAS. However, there are some inaccuracies regarding the tax rate and indexation benefits for LTCG on property after recent budget changes.
